abstract: The Gilbert-Varshamov (GV) bound is a fundamental benchmark for the existence of error-correcting codes. For non-linear $q$-ary codes of code length $n$, its finite length form is known to admit a multiplicative improvement of order $\Theta(n)$. In contrast, for $q$-ary linear codes of arbitrary rates, the best previously known general improvement was only of order $\Theta(\sqrt n)$. This leaves open whether the algebraic constraint of linearity inherently prevents a linear-order refinement. We show that it does not. For every fixed prime power $q$ and relative distance $0<\delta<1-1/q$, we obtain a $\Theta(n)$-multiplicative improvement of the GV bound for $q$-ary linear codes of arbitrary rate, matching the corresponding result for nonlinear codes. Our proof is based on a simple change of viewpoint. Rather than requiring the initial random linear construction to contain no low-weight vectors, we allow $O(n)$ low-weight points, show that they are independent in the underlying projective space, and then eliminate all of them simultaneously at the cost of a single dimension. The key probabilistic ingredient is an exponential bound on nontrivial linear dependencies among low-weight vectors. We further show that this approach can be extended to quantum codes despite the symplectic self-orthogonality constraint. We obtain a $\Theta(n)$-multiplicative improvement of the quantum GV bound for every fixed $0<\delta<1-1/q^2$ satisfying $H_{q^2}(\delta)<1/2$. Thus, the same $\Theta(n)$ finite length improvement is applicable to both general linear structure and symplectic self-orthogonality.
hook: Linear codes beat the Gilbert-Varshamov bound by a factor of n, matching nonlinear codes.
summary: Linear error-correcting codes can exceed the classic Gilbert-Varshamov existence bound by a factor that grows in proportion to code length, as nonlinear codes already could. The proof starts from a random linear code, tolerates a linear number of short vectors, and removes them all by giving up one dimension. The same gain extends to quantum codes, but only for distances where the entropy condition H(delta) < 1/2 holds.
title: A $\Theta(n)$-Multiplicative Improvement of the Gilbert-Varshamov Bound for Linear and Quantum Codes
